subject: community-medicine
title: Anthropometric Indices: Waist-Hip Ratio, Broca Index and Body Fat

steps.title: Central adiposity and hypothalamic regulation
steps.tx: The regulation of systemic energy balance involves complex **hypothalamic appetite circuitry**, where leptin from adipose stores and ghrelin from the gastric fundus modulate arcuate nucleus pro-opiomelanocortin and neuropeptide Y neurons. In central obesity, chronic hyperinsulinaemia and leptin resistance disrupt satiety signalling, driving preferential accumulation of metabolically active visceral adipose tissue around mesenteric vessels and abdominal organs.
steps.say: Appetite hormones like leptin and ghrelin balance calorie intake in the brain. In obesity, leptin resistance disrupts fullness signals, driving visceral fat accumulation in the abdomen.

steps.title: Waist-hip ratio as a cardiovascular predictor
steps.tx: While generalised body weight correlates with joint strain, the **waist-hip ratio measurement** provides a vastly superior marker for cardiovascular disease mortality and metabolic syndrome. Calculated as waist circumference divided by maximum hip circumference, the World Health Organization defines significant central obesity at a ratio greater than zero point nine zero in men and greater than zero point eight five in women.
steps.say: Waist-hip ratio is calculated by dividing waist circumference by hip circumference. A ratio exceeding zero point nine in men or zero point eight five in women signals high heart disease risk.

steps.title: Standardized waist circumference measurement
steps.tx: Because ratio calculations can mask concurrent visceral and peripheral weight gain, standalone **waist circumference measurement** offers a simpler and more reliable field screening tool for visceral fat. Measured at the midpoint between the lower palpable margin of the lowest rib and the top of the iliac crest in the mid-axillary line at end-expiration, action thresholds for Asian Indians are set at ninety centimetres for men and eighty centimetres for women.
steps.say: Measure waist size midway between the lowest rib and hip bone at gentle expiration. A waist over ninety centimetres in Indian men or eighty centimetres in women signals dangerous visceral fat.

steps.title: Quetelet index: body mass index formula
steps.tx: The most widely utilized epidemiological index of general adiposity is the **Quetelet index calculation**, universally known as the body mass index. Formulated by Adolphe Quetelet, it is computed as an individual's weight in kilograms divided by the square of their height in metres; while it provides a convenient population-level metric, it cannot distinguish lean muscle mass from adipose tissue in athletes.
steps.say: The Quetelet index, or body mass index, divides body weight in kilograms by height in metres squared. It estimates overall body size but cannot distinguish dense muscle from fat.

rows: Lowered for high percentage body fat

steps.title: Broca index for ideal body weight
steps.tx: A historic clinical shortcut frequently utilized for rapid bedside estimation of ideal weight is the **Broca index estimation**. For adult men, ideal body weight in kilograms is estimated as standing height in centimetres minus one hundred; for adult women, the formula subtracts one hundred and five (or height minus one hundred times zero point nine), providing a quick target for patient weight-loss goals.
steps.say: The Broca index estimates ideal weight by subtracting one hundred from standing height in centimetres for men, or one hundred and five for women. It gives a simple bedside weight goal.

rows: Used to calculate daily basal calorie targets

steps.title: Corpulence index and Ponderal index
steps.tx: To better account for three-dimensional body volume in taller and shorter subjects, anthropometrists utilize the **Corpulence index formula**, also known as the Rohrer index or Ponderal index. Calculated as body weight in kilograms divided by height in metres cubed (or height divided by the cube root of weight), it provides superior assessment of body proportionality in paediatric growth monitoring, foetal intrauterine growth restriction, and neonatal body symmetry.
steps.say: The Corpulence index divides weight by height cubed. By considering volume instead of area, it accurately assesses body proportionality in newborn infants and growing children.

steps.title: Skinfold thickness and subcutaneous fat measurement
steps.tx: Direct clinical quantification of subcutaneous adipose reserves relies on **skinfold thickness calliper measurement**, using calibrated spring-loaded callipers such as the Harpenden or Holtain callipers exerting a constant pressure of ten grams per square millimetre. Measurements are typically obtained over the triceps, biceps, subscapular and suprailiac sites on the non-dominant arm, with triceps skinfold exceeding twenty millimetres in men or thirty in women denoting obesity.
steps.say: Calibrated callipers pinch skinfolds on the triceps, shoulder blade and abdomen to measure body fat. A triceps skinfold over twenty millimetres in men indicates excess fat reserves.

Just below inferior angle of scapula at 45 deg
Just above iliac crest in mid-axillary line

steps.title: Densitometry and bioelectrical impedance
steps.tx: Advanced laboratory methods assess body composition through **bioelectrical impedance analysis**, measuring the opposition to a painless, low-voltage alternating electric current passing through bodily tissues. Because lean body mass contains water and electrolytes that conduct electricity freely while fat acts as an insulator, the machine computes total body water, fat-free mass, and percentage body fat, establishing that healthy adult body fat should remain below twenty-five percent in men.
steps.say: Bioelectrical impedance sends a gentle current through the body. Because water in muscle conducts electricity while fat resists it, the device precisely calculates total body fat percentage.

steps.title: Comprehensive obesity management hierarchy
steps.tx: Clinical management of obesity structures interventions through a stepped **obesity management hierarchy** beginning with dietary calorie deficits of five hundred to one thousand kilocalories daily and regular physical exercise. Pharmacotherapy with orlistat or GLP-1 receptor agonists like liraglutide is considered for BMI exceeding twenty-seven with comorbidities, while bariatric metabolic surgery is indicated for Asian Indians with BMI exceeding thirty-five, or thirty-two point five with severe uncontrolled diabetes.
steps.say: Obesity care starts with cutting five hundred calories daily and exercising. Medications are added if BMI exceeds twenty-seven, while bariatric surgery is offered for BMI over thirty-two point five.
